observations.observation_text: AWS IAM policies are objects that define permissions when associated with an identity or resource, and most policies are stored as JSON documents.
observations.rationale: Records the documented IAM policy object format without measurement language.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions

observations.observation_text: Identity-based policies are permissions policies attached to IAM identities such as users, groups, or roles.
observations.rationale: Records one documented policy category without comparative conclusions.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions
observations.source_location: Policies and permissions in IAM > Policy types, retrieved state
observations.observation_text: Resource-based policies are permissions policies attached to resources, and supported examples include IAM role trust policies and Amazon S3 bucket policies.
observations.rationale: Records a documented policy attachment category only.

observations.observation_text: When a principal makes a request, AWS gathers request information into a request context and uses it to evaluate applicable policies.
observations.rationale: Records the documented request-context processing step without deriving a measurement.

observations.source_type: Official product documentation (vendor/project docs) and reference architecture descriptions

observations.observation_text: AWS enforcement code evaluates applicable policy types and processes the policies against the request context to determine whether a request is allowed or denied.
